entities.label: Person
entities.summary: Francesco Armellini Pantalassi de' Medici was a cardinal of the Roman Catholic Church, born into a prominent Florentine family in 1469. He rose through the ranks of the Church, becoming a trusted advisor to Pope Clement VII and playing a key role in the papal politics of the late 16th century. Pantalassi de' Medici's influence extended beyond the Vatican, as he collaborated with other powerful figures of the time, including the Holy Roman Emperor Charles V. His legacy continued long after his death in 1528, as he helped shape the course of the Counter-Reformation and the Catholic Church's response to the Protestant Reformation. The striking quote, 'The Church is the pillar that holds up the world,' attributed to Pantalassi de' Medici, remains a testament to his enduring impact on Western Christianity.
